changes.text: The grants of a signed in user are refreshed every time the page is loaded, so new grants (for example Article.Read) show their administration links without signing in again.

Articles: public pages with a title, a short content and a content, grouped in their own article categories (with a header image) and searchable by title and content. Like news they are versioned with drafts, publishing, history, soft delete, restore and permanent delete for developers, but they cannot be scheduled, highlighted or commented. Read them at Articles, manage them under Administration (Article.Read, Article.Write, Article.Delete grants).

News, news categories and news comments are versioned like sites: every save inserts a new version and never changes an old one. News can be saved as a draft or published, an older version can be loaded into the editor or made live again, and the news list shows the live version only. The Ids of these entities are versioned keys.

News comments can be edited in place by their author and by holders of the News.Manage grant (administrators today, moderators when that role exists); an edited comment shows when it was edited, taken from the audit log.

Scheduled news: scheduling is optional, a news has no schedule by default and is shown as soon as it is published. With a schedule the news has a start and an optional end and is shown on the News page, opened and commented only while it is running; managers see every news with a Scheduled or Expired badge, and the news list is ordered by the start time (or the creation time without a schedule).

Highlighted news: a news can be flagged as highlighted and is then shown at the top of the news list; only one news can be highlighted, highlighting another one moves the highlight, and deleting a news removes its highlight.

News: a public News page lists the news, newest first and paged, each with its title, rich short content, author, the time it was created or last updated and its category; opening a news shows its rich content, or its short content when no content was written. The created and updated times are taken from the audit log.
News categories with a name and a header image uploaded in the administration; the News page can be filtered by category and shows the category header image.
Signed in users can comment on news; comments are paged, authors can delete their own comments and holders of the News.Delete grant can delete any comment.

News and news categories administration with the new News grant area (administration only): rich text editing with image uploads, search, first letter filter and paging, deleting, and for developers listing deleted records, restoring them and deleting them permanently.
The application starts when Security:Jwt is not configured, as the authorization services are always registered.

Licenses page linked from the footer: Behind is licensed under GPL-2.0-or-later and the page lists every frontend library, server package and development tool with its version, license and copyright, linking to the license texts.
LICENSE file with the GNU General Public License version 2 (or later) and the project copyright notice; the build properties declare the same license expression.
Confirming an email no longer ends with an incomplete link message after it succeeded; the link parameters are cleared without running the page a second time.
Sign-up sends a confirmation email with a link, and the link confirms the email address.
Email confirmation can be turned off with Security:EmailConfirmation (default true); when off, new emails are confirmed at the moment of sign-up.
Sign-up now sends (and logs) the confirmation email; the logger email sender also logs the email body when the environment is Development.
Passwordless sign-in with Magic Links, including rate limiting and security policies.
Sign-up, profile and display name management.
Session management: view the current session, list all sessions and sign out everywhere.
Role management and fine-grained access control for users and roles.
Administration area with user management: ban, unban, delete and permanently delete users.
Wall of shame listing banned users with their reason and expiry.
Elevation for sensitive operations.
Impersonation of other users, recorded in the audit log on their behalf.
Audit log with filtering, searching and paging.
Site administration: sites with a title, an editable slug and rich content (with image uploads), saved as versions that stay drafts until published, with one active version served in the wild.
Public sites are served at /<slug>, with /site/<slug> as the fallback for slugs that match built-in pages.
Sites can be searched, filtered by first letter and paged, deleted, restored and permanently deleted, like users.
Roles can be searched, filtered by first letter and paged, and deleted roles can be restored or permanently deleted by developers.
A custom index site: frontend.json can name a site slug that is shown at #/, and the Sites pages mark it.
The maximum site image size is configurable in frontend.json.
Active versions are stored in their own database context, as they are shared by every versioned entity.
Changes to frontend.json (site settings, image size limit, index site) are picked up without restarting the application.
The Stop impersonating button is visible in the dark theme.
Versioned keys now support Guid and text keys and keep their version when converted to text.
The audit log shows names (users, roles, grants, emails and so on) instead of raw identifiers.
Email confirmation tracking and an email sender with templates.
Footer with the application name and version, and this changelog page.
Frontend views now use Bootstrap, including automatic light and dark themes.
Requests are logged with correlation ids, and ETag support was added to the Web API.
Sensitive configuration values are masked, and data protection keys are protected by a certificate.
